quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungary, sunflowers are called 'napraforgó,' which literally means 'sun-turner' because the flower heads follow the sun across the sky during the day. Hungary is actually one of the world's largest producers of sunflower seeds, with vast golden fields that bloom in late summer.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: These tiny jewels of the bird world have hearts that beat up to 1,200 times per minute and can fly backwards. Learn about the amazing hummingbirds that visit Pacific Northwest gardens each summer.

medium_read.title: The Women Who Mapped the Ocean Floor
medium_read.teaser: Marie Tharp's hand-drawn maps in the 1950s revealed underwater mountains and valleys no one knew existed, changing our understanding of Earth forever. Her story is one of persistence, curiosity, and scientific breakthrough.

long_read.title: The Wisdom of Old-Growth Forests
long_read.teaser: Ancient trees in the Pacific Northwest hold secrets about communication, cooperation, and survival that scientists are only beginning to understand. This fascinating exploration reveals how forests are more connected than we ever imagined.

port_angeles.title: Roosevelt Elk at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot Roosevelt elk grazing in the meadows at Hurricane Ridge. These magnificent animals, named after President Theodore Roosevelt, are native to the Olympic Peninsula and can weigh up to 1,000 pounds. Early morning or late afternoon offers the best viewing opportunities.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's wings can beat up to ___ times per second.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Wonderful! That's right — 80 beats per second creates that distinctive humming sound we hear when they zip by!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 80 times per second — that incredible speed creates their humming sound!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 80 times per second! That's what creates the humming sound that gives them their name.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the fastest wing-beat of any bird, and they're the only birds that can fly backwards and even upside down. Their heart rate can reach 1,200 beats per minute during flight!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's absolutely right — a beautiful word you probably use often!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'köszönöm'! Szia means 'hi,' viszlát means 'goodbye,' and igen means 'yes.'
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language in Europe, part of the Finno-Ugric family rather than Indo-European. It's considered one of the most difficult languages to learn because of its complex grammar and 18 grammatical cases!

puzzle_3.question: What is the Strait of Juan de Fuca named after?
options: A Greek navigator who sailed for Spain
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfectly done! Juan de Fuca was actually a Greek navigator named Ioannis Phokas who sailed under a Spanish name in 1592!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It was named after a Greek navigator named Ioannis Phokas who sailed under the Spanish name Juan de Fuca in 1592. He claimed to have discovered the passage between the Pacific Ocean and the inland sea.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The strait you can see from Port Angeles connects the Pacific Ocean to Puget Sound and the Salish Sea. It's about 96 miles long and forms part of the border between Washington State and Vancouver Island, British Columbia.
